rows.description: A student who asks a basic question in class, unashamed, learns faster than one who nods and hides confusion. Humility is the entry fee for real learning.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague notices someone say I am nothing while fishing for praise. Humble-bragging asks for attention by pretending not to, and it is usually detected.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child realises that a sibling who broke a toy was scared and not mean. Perspective-taking at this age is real but effortful and often fades under anger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager quarrelling with a parent can only see their side, though calm afterwards they understand the parent's fear. Emotion narrows the view, and wisdom includes waiting until it widens.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A grandparent's account of hardship and choices gives a teenager a longer timeline for their own troubles. Stories across generations carry perspective that advice alone cannot.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult facing a disaster asks how much it will matter in a year, and to whom. Zooming out in time and space cuts drama without denying pain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teacher sees a brilliant student win arguments yet make poor life choices. Intelligence handles problems, while wisdom weighs what is worth pursuing and at what cost.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult facing a decision consults people who have lived through something similar, and weighs their view against their own values. Wise people ask widely and still decide themselves.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child hands over a toy after a parent's urging, yet feels the loss keenly. Genuine generosity begins as imitation and becomes real only when it is not forced.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child gives half a tiffin to a hungry classmate without being told, feeling warm afterwards. Freely chosen giving builds an identity as a generous person.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 18–22, 23–26
